ko.executive_summary: AI data center demand is accelerating optical interconnect adoption, with Marvell leading advanced optical initiatives and Samsung/SK Hynix entering the CPO race. Semiconductor laser and optical transceiver markets are expanding through 2035 driven by bandwidth requirements for data center-scale AI deployment.
key_facts: Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) advancing optical interconnect for AI data centers
Samsung and SK Hynix entering CPO (Co-Packaged Optics) market
Optical transceiver modules and semiconductor laser markets growing to 2035
Data center intra-connectivity shifting to optical 'speed of light' paradigm for AI workloads

implications.text: Korean and U.S. semiconductor leaders (Samsung, SK, Marvell) converging on CPO as strategic differentiation; competition intensifying beyond traditional transceiver suppliers.
Marvell's 2nm optical roadmap signals aggressive scaling of optical chiplets; likely to enable higher density co-packaging with compute dies.
AI model inference/training bandwidth bottlenecks are shifting investment from compute-centric to optical-interconnect-centric semiconductor architectures.
Optical intra-data center connectivity becoming standard rather than niche; impacts switch, NIC, and transceiver vendor positioning.

ko.counterpoint: Headlines lack specifics on transceiver speed targets (e.g., 800G, 1.6T), shipping timelines, or volume commitments; market projections to 2035 may not account for disruptive interconnect alternatives.
